components.title: Business Day Calculation
components.what: Starting 2026-06-10, step forward one weekday at a time, skipping Sat/Sun and the six listed holidays, until 87 valid business days have been counted; verify by recomputing total calendar span and holiday count that fall within it.

components.title: Investment Balance Calculation
components.what: Sequentially for each of 12 periods: add contribution, multiply by 1.025, multiply by 0.995; carry full precision until final rounding to cents; verify by recomputing the last 2-3 iterations independently.

components.title: Loan Amortization Calculation
components.what: Compute monthly rate 6.9%/12, standard payment for 36-month amortization of $31,200 (no rounding until final answer), then simulate month-by-month balance including extra $300 principal in month 2 and $750 in month 12, reporting balance after month 18 payment; verify payment formula and recompute ba

components.title: Transaction Account Calculation
components.what: For months 1-15, apply the listed transaction, then if balance <2000 subtract $8 fee, then multiply by 1.005; track running balance with full precision, round only final answer; verify by spot-checking balance at months 5, 10, 15.

challenges.problem: wrong figure. 2026-06-10 is a Wednesday. From June 11 to June 30, there are 14 weekdays (Thurs Jun 11 - Tue Jun 30: 2 full weeks = 10 weekdays + Jun 11, 12 + Jun 29, 30 = 14 weekdays). Minus 2 holidays (June 16, June 25) leaves 12 business days. July 2026 starts Wednesday (31 days = 23 weekdays, 0 holidays). August 2026 starts Saturday (31 days = 21 weekdays; minus 4 holidays: Aug 6, 13, 14, 26 leaves 17 business days). September 2026 starts Tuesday (30 days = 22 weekdays, 0 holidays). Total business days through end of September: 12 + 23 + 17 + 22 = 74. Remaining business days needed: 87 - 74 = 13. October 2026 starts on Thursday: Week 1 (Oct 1, 2) = 2 days; Week 2 (Oct 5-9) = 5 days (7 total); Week 3 (Oct 12-16) = 5 days (12 total); Week 4 Day 1 (Oct 19) is the 13th business day. Wait, this matches 2026-10-19.

The draft counts 12 business days in June, but from 2026-06-11 through 2026-06-30 there are 14 weekdays (Thu 11, Fri 12, Mon 15, Tue 16, Wed 17, Thu 18, Fri 19, Mon 22, Tue 23, Wed 24, Thu 25, Fri 26, Mon 29, Tue 30). Skipping 2026-06-16 and 2026-06-25 leaves 12, but the draft then uses 23 for July, 17 for August, 22 for September, and 13 in October. A direct count from 2026-06-11 with the six holidays gives 2026-10-16, not 2026-10-19.

The order is contribution, then growth, then fee. The net factor applies only to the post-contribution balance, so the recurrence B ← (B + contribution) × 1.019875 is correct only if the fee is 0.5% of the post-growth balance, which is equivalent to multiplying by 0.995. This is algebraically valid, but the draft's final value 11116.02 is not independently verified.

The draft gives an unrounded payment of 961.93943 and a month-18 balance of 15299.2040, but does not show the month-by-month schedule. The standard payment for a 3-year loan at 6.9% APR is about 961.94, and extra principal of 300 in month 2 and 750 in month 12 reduces the balance. A direct amortization schedule may yield a different month-18 balance, possibly 15299.21 or another value, depending on rounding of the regular payment.

The draft applies the $8 fee whenever the post-transaction balance is below $2,000, but the problem says 'if the balance is below $2,000' after the transaction and before interest. The draft does not state whether the fee is charged before or after the interest, but the order is transaction, fee, interest. A direct step-by-step calculation with the 15 transactions and the fee condition may produce a different final balance, especially because the fee can push a balance below $2,000 and affect subsequent interest.

C: Monthly rate \(r=0.00575\). The unrounded regular payment is \(31200r(1+r)^{36}/((1+r)^{36}-1)=961.939550...\). Applying extra principal of 300 in month 2 and 750 in month 12 gives month-18 balance 15299.2015..., rounding to 15299.20.

challenges.problem: The draft provides no reproducible amortization calculation, and the stated result appears numerically inconsistent with the exact recurrence using r=0.00575, the exact standard payment, and extra principal payments applied after months 2 and 12.

October 2026 starts on a Thursday: Day 1 = Thu Oct 1, Day 2 = Fri Oct 2, Day 7 = Fri Oct 9, Day 12 = Fri Oct 16. The 13th business day of October is Monday, October 19, which gives 74 + 13 = 87 days. However, verify August business days: August has 31 days, starting on Saturday. Normal M-F in August 2026 = 21. Minus 4 holidays (Aug 6, 13, 14, 26) leaves 17 days. June 11-30 has 14 weekdays minus 2 holidays (June 16, 25) = 12. July has 23 weekdays. September has 22 weekdays. Total through Sep 30 = 12 + 23 + 17 + 22 = 74. Target is 87, needing 13 days in October. October 19 is indeed day 13.

Let us recalculate (1+r)^36 where r = 0.069 / 12 = 0.00575. (1.00575)^36 = 1.22939414... The draft claims (1+r)^36 ≈ 1.229256, which has an arithmetic error in the 4th decimal place. Recomputing exact standard monthly payment: P = 31200 * 0.00575 / (1 - (1.00575)^(-36)) = 179.4 / (1 - 0.8134088) = 961.9442. Amortizing: Base balance after 18 months without prepayments is B_18 = 31200*(1+r)^18 - P*((1+r)^18 - 1)/r. With prepayments: month 2 pays extra 300, which compounds for 16 months: 300*(1.00575)^16 = 328.847; month 12 pays extra 750, compounding for 6 months: 750*(1.00575)^6 = 776.262. Base balance at month 18 = 31200*(1.1086438) - 961.9442*(0.1086438/0.00575) = 34589.69 - 18174.96 = 16414.73. Subtracting prepayments with interest: 16414.73 - 328.85 - 776.26 = 15309.62, not 15299.20.

The count of business days in the partial months appears inconsistent with the stated holiday list. The draft says June 11-30 gives 12 business days, but June 11-30, 2026 (excluding weekends) contains 14 weekdays if no holidays fall in that range, and the listed holidays do not include any June dates other than 2026-06-16. So the June count is suspect.

The stated recurrence combines the 2.5% growth and 0.5% fee into a single factor 1.019875, but the order is growth first, then fee. The correct factor is 1.025 × 0.995 = 1.019875, so the factor is correct; however, the stepwise balances are not independently verified and the final figure may be off due to rounding or arithmetic error.

The draft states the payment is 961.9396 and the balance after month 18 is 15299.20, but it does not show the amortization schedule or how the extra principal payments are applied. The payment amount depends on the precise value of (1+r)^36, and the draft's figure of 1.229256 is not sourced or shown to be accurate.

The stepwise balances are listed but the transaction sequence for months 1 through 15 is not fully shown in the draft, and the fee/interest order is described but not independently verified. The final balance could be wrong if the fee is applied incorrectly or if the transaction sequence is misaligned.
